entries.intro: Thin week for net-new sourcing. The strongest names are Rove (building its own loyalty stack), Revolut (airline currency links for fintech wallets), Etihad (new US co-brand), plus a few experience and dining plays. Most Bilt and Chase stories are competitor moves to benchmark, not partner leads.

items.what: Travel rewards platform with its own points currency, travel portal, dining program and a growing list of transfer partners (launched about 18 months ago).
items.signal: Launched an elite status program with up to every third hotel night free, plus shopping and transfer bonuses.
items.why_fit: It is assembling a full loyalty stack quickly, which makes it a candidate for hotel perks, transfer access or offers aimed at affluent travelers.
items.angle: Hotel night or portal benefit for premium cardholders, or a transfer-partner link into its currency.

items.what: Fintech account provider that now gives customers access to the Velocity airline loyalty currency.
items.signal: Revolut customers can now access Velocity Points, linking the fintech to an airline loyalty program.
items.why_fit: Shows non-bank wallets are getting direct airline loyalty links, which is a competitive route to affluent travelers and a model for transfer-style deals.
items.angle: Track how the Revolut link is structured and consider whether a similar airline loyalty tie-in could sit alongside our rewards currency.

items.what: Gulf airline with a premium long-haul product and loyalty program.
items.signal: Launched its first US credit cards, one with instant airline status and airport lounge access. Issuer not stated in the item.
items.why_fit: A premium international carrier entering the US card market signals appetite for US issuer partnerships and a status-plus-lounge value proposition.
items.angle: Etihad status or lounge benefit for a premium card, or a Gulf and Middle East travel perk. Confirm the issuer and exclusivity first.

items.what: Global hotel group launching its first paid membership.
items.signal: The paid membership targets local diners rather than hotel guests, with generous discounts.
items.why_fit: A hotel brand building a local-spend product opens card-linked dining and local-experience angles, not just travel.
items.angle: Complimentary or discounted membership as a cardholder dining and hotel benefit, tied to everyday local spend.

items.what: Ski pass product now redeemable with Alaska Atmos points (65K for Ikon Base, 100K for the full pass).
items.signal: Alaska's Atmos Unlocked lets members spend points on Ikon ski passes.
items.why_fit: Points-for-experience redemption in a high-income lifestyle category (skiing) is a template for non-travel redemption options.
items.angle: Ski or outdoor pass as a redemption or statement-credit style benefit for affluent cardholders.

items.what: Network-level entertainment partnership between Disney and Visa.
items.signal: Visa cardholders get early entry to Hong Kong Disneyland under the new deal.
items.why_fit: Early-entry access is a low-cost, high-perceived-value perk that appeals to affluent families, and it is a competitor-network play worth countering.
items.angle: Theme-park early entry or priority access benefit negotiated at the issuer level in US destinations. Confirm which networks and cards are covered.

items.what: Restaurant reservation platform whose rewards program pays an extra 4X Membership Rewards points on dining.
items.signal: Resy Rewards now adds 4X Membership Rewards points on dining for eligible cardholders.
items.why_fit: It is an active issuer-linked dining program and a direct benchmark for what a restaurant reservation partner can do for card spend.
items.angle: Reservation-platform dining earn or credit for Wells Fargo cardholders, or a competing arrangement with another reservation platform.

items.what: Travel eSIM data provider behind a card-linked benefit (15 days, 5GB).
items.signal: US Bank confirmed its Altitude Connect GigSky eSIM benefit may end on November 30, 2026.
items.why_fit: A benefit sunset leaves a gap for travel-data perks, and eSIM roaming is a practical, low-cost benefit for international travelers.
items.angle: eSIM travel data allowance as a lower-cost international travel perk on a premium card.

entries.intro: A moderate week: a few real partner-style plays (Resy, Oura, Rove, Qantas and Cathay) plus one rising rival to watch (Bilt). Several items are copycat or counter plays, not net-new partners, so only the ones worth a team conversation made the cut.

items.what: Reservation platform that Amex owns, now paired with a reservation-linked rewards program.
items.signal: Amex launched Resy Rewards, giving 4 extra Membership Rewards points on dining reservations paid with an enrolled card. Restaurant eligibility looks limited and rollout is unclear.
items.why_fit: Ties card earn directly to booking behavior at restaurants affluent clients favor, and could be replicated with a non-Amex reservation or dining platform.
items.angle: A reservation-linked dining earn or access perk with a booking partner, positioned as a counter to Resy Rewards.

items.what: Maker of the Oura smart ring, a premium wearable.
items.signal: Oura Ring 5 is $299 in an early Black Friday sale, and Amex Platinum cardholders can bring it to $99 plus tax through November 30 via a card benefit. Sale end date and credit eligibility are not fully confirmed.
items.why_fit: A premium wellness hardware brand with a proven card-credit structure and strong fit with affluent, health-minded clients.
items.angle: A wellness or wearable statement credit or member price, positioned as a counter to the Platinum Oura offer.

items.what: Shopping offers platform that pays out in airline miles.
items.signal: Rove launched personalized shopping offers paying up to 25 miles per dollar spent.
items.why_fit: A card-linked or miles-linked offer engine could supply merchant offers without us building each merchant relationship one by one.
items.angle: Personalized merchant offers surfaced to premium cardholders, or a benchmark for our own offers strategy.

items.what: Rent-focused rewards platform and card program, now pushing into travel and events.
items.signal: Reportedly seeking an $18 billion valuation, and its December Rent Day adds a JetBlue Mosaic status challenge and a redemption bonus up to 100%. The valuation talks are unconfirmed.
items.why_fit: A fast-growing rival building partner-funded perks (airline status, concerts, redemption bonuses) aimed at younger affluent renters, a segment partners will chase.
items.angle: Partner-funded status matches or lifestyle events for renters and younger affluent clients, and a rival to track for partner overlap.

items.what: Global hotel loyalty program and a major US airline.
items.signal: Hyatt plans stackable awards, new Milestone Rewards and Delta perks, all launching in 2027.
items.why_fit: A hotel and airline tie-up signals where affluent travelers' loyalty is consolidating, and Hyatt has a strong premium guest base.
items.angle: Complementary hotel or airline benefits timed ahead of the 2027 rollout.

items.what: Private aviation provider offering fractional ownership and jet cards.
items.signal: NetJets was named official private aviation provider for the Hahnenkamm Races in Kitzbühel.
items.why_fit: A premium event sponsorship shows appetite for affluent audience reach, which suits top-tier card flight and experience benefits.
items.angle: Private aviation access or event-linked flight benefit for top-tier cardholders.

items.what: Bill-pay fintech that lets businesses pay bills by card for a 2.9% fee and earn transferable points.
items.signal: Adding Atmos Rewards support soon, which is not yet live.
items.why_fit: Turns otherwise uncardable business spend into points, relevant to small business and affluent owner clients.
items.angle: Business bill-pay earn partnership for premium business cardholders.
